primitives.name: Hintikka Verification-Falsification Games
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Hintikka verification-falsification (VF) game semantics adapted to markets: an asset for ∃x.P(x) is an option to exchange it for a finite conjunction ∧_{x∈S}P(x); for ∀x.P(x) an obligation against the opponent's finite choice.

primitives.name: Polynomial-Time Agent Market Equilibrium
primitives.verbatim_quote: A "program market" of polynomial-time agents (trader + player + labeler + inventory), with an equilibrium price setter ̟ defined as the zero of aggregate excess demand; ̟'s player counters the aggregate agent's players on P vs ¬P so it wins exactly as many games as it loses.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'̟': 'Equilibrium price function', 'P': 'Logical proposition', '¬P': 'Negation of P', 'aggregate excess demand': 'Sum of individual trader demands'}
primitives.assumptions: Agents operate within polynomial-time constraints; equilibrium arises from zero excess demand.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Asymptotic convergence fails for non-computable or highly complex logical structures.

layer2.mapping: Market equilibrium mirrors GSE's dynamic pricing engine under bounded rationality constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Price stability over time and agent counter-strategy balance

primitives.name: Constructive Truth Convergence
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions Key results: Lemma 1.2 (no computable asset/scoring-rule mechanism exists for Σ4/Π4+ sentences — Tarski's theorem); Lemma 3.1 (inexploitability of ̟); Theorem 3.2 (equilibrium prices converge for every sentence); Theorem 3.4/ Corollary 3.5 (market learns "constructive truth": if P is computably-verifiable-true then ̟^∞(P)=1).

primitives.assumptions: Market prices reflect truth when computable verification is possible; otherwise, they remain undefined.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-computable or undecidable logical sentences beyond Tarski’s limits.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in adapting Hintikka’s VF game semantics to prediction markets for non-verifiable logical sentences. This allows modeling belief updates through adversarial play rather than empirical resolution. The framework defines assets as options or obligations based on quantifier types (∃ vs ∀), enabling a market structure where traders must resolve logical ambiguity through strategic interaction. Polynomial-time agents simulate this process, with equilibrium prices emerging as solutions to aggregate excess demand functions. Key theorems show convergence for all sentences but fail for Σ4/Π4+ due to Tarski’s incompleteness. Constructive truth emerges as a limiting property: if a sentence is computably verifiable, its long-run price converges to 1. However, these insights lack operational mapping to GSE’s domain of Δ0-verifiable sports outcomes, which require fixed-time resolution and empirical validation. Thus, while mathematically elegant, the framework cannot support GSE’s real-time market microstructure or calibration needs.
